subject: Capacity augmentation & scale-safeguard playbook (renewal)
messages:
From: Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal questions: capacity uplift & throughput guarantees

Evelyn / Marissa,

We’re starting the renewal conversation for our Dedicated cluster that supports our customer-facing search and suggestions. Usage has grown faster than we forecasted — attached is the current consumption and some spike days (Acme_Renewal_Status.xlsx).

High level asks from our side:
- Reserve additional capacity: +8 GPUs (A100-similar) to be held as part of our dedicated pool.
- Warm pool / pre-bake: we want a warm standby to reduce cold-start impact during spikes.
- Throughput guarantee: target sustained 300–350 requests/sec during business hours with clear remediation steps if SLOs slip.
- Clarify scale-up lag expectations — we saw 60–90s cold starts previously and need a faster recovery.

Can Redwood put together a short playbook (configuration + term addendum language + pricing delta) that we can review before the legal/finance loop? We have an initial renewal window in late March.

Thanks,
Jane
Head of Infrastructure
Acme Industries

Attachment: Acme_Renewal_Status.xlsx

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions: capacity uplift & throughput guarantees

Jane — thanks for the detail and the file. We can absolutely support a dedicated uplift and a formalized scale-safeguard playbook. I’m attaching an initial draft (capacity_playbook_v1.pdf) so you and your infra team can see concrete options.

Quick summary of the options in the draft:
- Option A (balanced): +8 reserved GPUs; min_replicas=2, max_replicas=10; warm_pool=2 replicas; target scale_up_lag ~45s (p50) with warm pool, ~90s cold otherwise. Throughput guard: 320 rps sustained for 95% of 1-hour windows.
- Option B (aggressive): +8 reserved GPUs; min_replicas=3, max_replicas=12; warm_pool=3 replicas; prebake 40% of keys for common prefixes; target scale_up_lag <=30s (p95) when warm_pool active. Higher reserved fee but lower burst cost.

Notes:
- Warm pool reduces scale-up latency but has a reserved cost component; we show trade-offs in the attachment.
- We can add an explicit SLA clause for throughput remediation (crediting and escalation path) if you want that baked into the term addendum.

Next steps I propose: 1) pick Option A or B (or hybrid), 2) pick term length (12 vs 24 months) — pricing materially changes at 24 months, 3) we circulate SOW + addendum.

I’ve looped Marissa for commercial terms and Karthik for a quick technical note on scale metrics.

— Evelyn
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_playbook_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@acme.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions: capacity uplift & throughput guarantees

Jane — appreciate the clear asks. Below are concrete commercial and configuration proposals you can take back to finance:

Commercial / term (proposal):
- Reserved uplift: 8 GPUs added to your Dedicated pool.
- Term options: 12-month (baseline) or 24-month (15% reserved discount + committed burst credits).
- Pricing structure we will include in SOW: monthly reserved fee + fractional GPU-hour charge for bursts beyond reserved pool + per-GB egress as currently contracted.

Operational configuration (recommended baseline):
- min_replicas: 2
- max_replicas: 12
- warm_pool: 3 replicas (hot standby)
- prebake: 35% of inferred hot prefixes into KV cache for the first 100 tokens
- scale_up_lag target (observability-backed): p50 <= 15s when warm_pool is active, p95 <= 30s; cold-path p95 <= 90s
- throughput guarantee: sustained 320 rps for 95% of rolling 1-hour windows; remediation: 10% service credit for breach + 1:1 architecture review within 48 hours.

Operational notes & fallbacks:
- We'll include automatic fallback routing to a compatible quantized model in the same region during severe capacity stress to keep user-facing latency within acceptable bands.
- Warm pool sizing is tunable; if your latency spikes persist we can increase warm_pool to 4 at a marginal incremental reserved fee.

Action items for Acme: please indicate preferred term (12/24) and whether you want the additional SLA language in the contract. I’ll draft the SOW and the addendum after that.

— Marissa
Enterprise Renewal Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_draft_ACME.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@acme.com>
Date: 2028-03-05T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions: capacity uplift & throughput guarantees — technical note

Quick technical clarifications from the infra side:
- The p95 <= 30s scale_up_lag target when warm_pool active is achievable if we: 1) maintain warm_pool replicas with hot KV caches, and 2) pre-allocate session slots on the reserved GPUs (pre-baked process).
- Measured data attached (scale_metrics_snapshot.csv) shows that with a 3-replica warm pool and prebake of the top 30% prefixes, median cold-start is ~12s, p95 ~28s under synthetic load.
- For your traffic profile I recommend we enable prefix-based caching + an adaptive warm_pool policy (auto-increase to 4 on sustained 15% above baseline traffic for >30 minutes). That keeps costs lower while ensuring headroom.

If you want, we can ship a final benchmark run against your representative trace before sign.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Attachment: scale_metrics_snapshot.csv

From: Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-07T11:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions: capacity uplift & throughput guarantees

Thanks — this looks good and much more actionable than our initial ask. A few follow-ups from finance/legal:
- We’re inclined to do 24 months if the 15% reserved discount is firm and the throughput SLA is explicit in the addendum.
- For the scale-up lag we need the contract to state p95 <= 30s when warm_pool active, with a remediation path if that is missed.
- Also want the ability to burst an additional 4 GPUs for up to 72 hours in a calendar quarter without having to renegotiate pricing (we’re willing to pay a higher burst rate for those hours).

If you can incorporate those bullets into the SOW/addendum I can route to procurement next week. We’ll sign contingent on DocuSign link + acceptance of the SLA language.

— Jane
Head of Infrastructure
Acme Industries

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-09T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions: capacity uplift & throughput guarantees — final steps

Jane — great, thank you. We’ll proceed with the following and circulate the DocuSign package today:

Committed items (to be encoded in SOW + term addendum):
- Reserved uplift: +8 GPUs added to your Dedicated pool (24-month term, 15% reserved discount applied).
- Operational config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=12, warm_pool=3 (adaptive to 4), prebake ~35%.
- SLA excerpt: p95 scale_up_lag <= 30s when warm_pool active; throughput guarantee: sustained 320 rps for 95% of rolling 1-hour windows. Remediation: 10% service credit + architecture review within 48 hours for breaches.
- Burst allowance: additional +4 GPUs for up to 72 hours per quarter at burst rate; no contract renegotiation required for those events.

I’ve asked Legal to include explicit wording for the p95 metric and the burst allowance. You’ll receive a DocuSign link here: https://www.docusign.net/Sign?doc=ACME-RNW-17 — please review and sign; HubSpot record for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-12345.

If you want the benchmark run Karthik mentioned, we can schedule it for the week after signature. Once DocuSign is signed we’ll schedule a kickoff to implement the warm pool and prebake rules.

Thanks again — looking forward to closing this out.

— Evelyn
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
